codePractice.title: Two-Sum with Sorted Array
codePractice.instructions: Given a sorted array and target sum, return indices of the two numbers.
codePractice.solution: function twoSumSorted(arr, target) { let l=0, r=arr.length-1; while(l<r){ let s=arr[l]+arr[r]; if(s===target)return[l,r]; if(s<target)l++; else r--; } return null; }

codePractice.title: Inorder Traversal Simulation
codePractice.instructions: Simulate inorder traversal order for a simple tree object.
codePractice.solution: function inorder(root, res = []) { if (!root) return res; inorder(root.left, res); res.push(root.val); inorder(root.right, res); return res; }

lessons.title: 3. Dynamic Programming: 0/1 Knapsack & Memoization
lessons.summary: Transition equations, top-down memoization vs bottom-up tabulation, and space optimization tricks.

codePractice.title: Fibonacci with Memoization
codePractice.instructions: Calculate the N-th Fibonacci number in O(N) time using memoization.
codePractice.solution: function fibMemo(n, memo = {}) { if (n <= 1) return n; if (memo[n]) return memo[n]; return memo[n] = fibMemo(n - 1, memo) + fibMemo(n - 2, memo); }

questions.question: What will be the output of `console.log(typeof NaN)` in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, NaN is a numeric value representing 'Not-a-Number', so `typeof NaN` returns 'number'.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is idempotent and used to replace an entire resource in REST?
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent and replaces the target resource entirely. PATCH makes partial updates.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `next()` function in Express.js middleware?
options: Pass control to the next middleware function in stack
questions.explanation: The `next()` callback tells Express to proceed to the next matching middleware in the application pipeline.

questions.question: Which part of a JWT (JSON Web Token) contains the user payload and role information?
questions.explanation: The payload (second part of JWT) contains claims such as user ID, role, and expiration timestamp.

questions.question: In the Node.js event loop, which phase handles expired `setTimeout` callbacks?
questions.explanation: The Timers phase executes callbacks scheduled by `setTimeout()` and `setInterval()`.

questions.question: Which Python data type is immutable?
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable sequences in Python; their elements cannot be modified once created.

questions.question: In Supervised Learning, what does Overfitting typically indicate?
options: High training error and high test error
Low training error and high test error
Low training error and low test error
Model is too simple to capture patterns
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise from training data (low train error) and fails to generalize (high test error).

questions.question: What library in Python is primarily used for multi-dimensional array computing?
questions.explanation: NumPy provides high-performance N-dimensional array objects and mathematical operations.

forum.title: How does the Node.js event loop handle asynchronous file I/O versus network requests?
forum.author: Atul Mehta

replies.author: Dr. Priya Nair
replies.content: Great question! Network I/O is delegated directly to OS asynchronous system calls (like epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS, IOCP on Windows). In contrast, standard file system I/O does not have unified async OS interfaces across platforms, so Node.js offloads file system operations to the libuv threadpool (default 4 threads).

forum.title: What is the difference between Array and LinkedList memory allocation in Java?
forum.author: Karthik Verma

replies.author: Dr. Priya Nair
replies.content: Arrays allocate contiguous blocks of memory, which provides O(1) random access and excellent CPU cache locality. LinkedList allocates non-contiguous nodes on the heap with pointers (references), which incurs extra memory overhead per node and O(N) access time.
